draft.title: Independence and anti-conformity
card: Independence is making your own judgement and acting on it, even when others disagree. It is not the same as opposing the group for the sake of it.
Anti-conformity is deliberately doing the opposite of what a group does or expects. The group still shapes the choice, because the person is reacting to it.
Knowing how groups influence us helps people spot pressure when it happens. A person can then ask whether the group is right before going along.
Having even one other person who disagrees can make it easier to speak up. Checking evidence for yourself also helps people resist a group that is wrong.
draft.remember: Independence means thinking for yourself. Anti-conformity means doing the opposite of the group.

opts: Checking the facts, then voting as the evidence suggests
Voting against whatever the rest of the class votes for
Voting for whatever the most popular student votes for
Voting the same way as friends to avoid an argument
a.why: Independence means making your own judgement from the evidence, whatever the group does. Voting against the class every time is anti-conformity, because the group still decides the choice.
a.clue: Who or what is deciding the choice?

b.q: Everyone in Jin's team agrees to hand in a plan with a mistake Jin has spotted. Jin checks the figures, then tells them. Which idea does this show?
opts: Independence, as Jin uses evidence rather than the group
Anti-conformity, as Jin opposes the group on purpose
Obedience, as Jin follows an order to speak up
Conformity, as Jin matches what the team wants
b.why: Jin checked the evidence and acted on it, even though the group disagreed. That is independence. It is not anti-conformity, because Jin was not simply opposing the team for the sake of it.
b.clue: Why did Jin disagree with the team?

a.best: Checking the facts, then voting as the evidence suggests

b.best: Independence, as Jin uses evidence rather than the group
